implementation_statement: POL-02 Access Control (P06) was approved 2026-09-15, effective 2026-10-01, replacing the 2024 policy. Gap: the OT access procedure for HMIs and engineering workstations and the MES account procedure are due 2026-12-31 under STD-06.

Office accounts are provisioned in the identity provider from the HR system feed and disabled automatically at termination. ERP roles are reviewed quarterly. MES accounts at both plants are local badge-and-PIN accounts managed by plant administrators. Gaps: Plant 2 MES uses 3 shared supervisor override accounts; production MES accounts were disabled late in 6 of 25 sampled terminations (P07); MES and OT accounts are not in any access review (POAM-004).
evidence: IdP export; HR termination report; ERP quarterly review records; MES user lists

implementation_statement: Account lifecycle for office users is automated through the HR-driven identity provider workflow (create, disable, remove).
Identity provider accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled automatically. Gap: local MES and HMI accounts have no inactivity disablement (POAM-004).
evidence: IdP policy setting; MES user list

implementation_statement: Account creation, modification, and disabling events in the identity provider and the corporate directory are sent to the SIEM, and the MSSP alerts on new privileged accounts.
evidence: SIEM use case list; sample alert 2026-07

implementation_statement: ERP access is enforced through 61 role templates mapped to job functions. MES enforces station-level permissions. Gap: 7 ERP users hold super-user roles (target 3), and Plant 2 MES grants all supervisors recipe-reference edit rights.
evidence: ERP role catalog; super-user list; Plant 2 MES role export

implementation_statement: At Plant 1, the IT/OT firewall allows only defined flows between the ERP, integration platform, OT DMZ, and plant zones (deny by default since 2025). Gap: at Plant 2 the MES server is dual-homed and the office and plant networks are one routed space, so flows are not enforced (POAM-001).
evidence: Plant 1 firewall rule base; Plant 2 network diagram (draft); P07 SC-7 test

implementation_statement: ERP segregation-of-duties rules separate vendor master changes from payment approval and purchase order approval. Gap: 2 of the 7 ERP super users can do both; a compensating monthly review by the Controller started 2026-08.
evidence: ERP SoD conflict report 2026-07; Controller review sign-off

implementation_statement: Administrators use separate privileged accounts; cloud and domain administration goes through the privileged access broker with just-in-time elevation. Gaps: the Plant 2 MES service account is a member of the corporate Domain Admins group through the Plant 2 domain trust (P07 finding, R-051); OT engineering workstation accounts are local administrators everywhere (POAM-002, POAM-016).
evidence: Privileged account list (41 accounts); broker logs; P07 AC-6 test

implementation_statement: Access to security functions (EDR console, SIEM tenant, firewall management, identity provider administration) is limited to named security and infrastructure staff. Gap: Plant 2 firewall administration still uses a shared local account.
evidence: Console role exports; Plant 2 firewall account list

implementation_statement: Administrators use non-privileged accounts for email and web; privileged accounts are blocked from email and internet browsing by conditional access.
evidence: Conditional access policy; account naming standard

implementation_statement: Privileged accounts are limited to 41 named accounts across cloud, identity, directory, ERP, and network planes. Gap: the Plant 2 legacy domain has 6 administrator accounts outside the broker (POAM-002).

Use of privileged functions in the cloud, identity provider, and corporate directory is logged to the SIEM. Gap: MES administration and OT engineering workstation actions are not logged centrally (POAM-007).
The identity provider locks accounts after 10 failed attempts and applies risk-based throttling.
A system use notice is displayed at sign-in to the identity provider, the VPN, and MES kiosks.

Office endpoints lock after 15 minutes. Kiosks use shared station sessions by design with badge-and-PIN confirmation per transaction. Gap: 9 Plant 2 kiosks were found logged in under a supervisor account (P07).
ERP and identity provider sessions end after 12 hours or on sign-out; administrative sessions after 1 hour.

Office remote access uses the identity provider and an always-on VPN with device compliance. OEM remote access at Plant 1 goes through the remote access gateway with MFA, per-session approval, and recording. Gap: Plant 2 OEM access uses 4 always-on cellular routers with shared logins and no MFA or logging (POAM-003).
evidence: VPN configuration; gateway session records; P07 MA-4 walkthrough

implementation_statement: Remote sessions through the VPN and the Plant 1 gateway are logged and monitored by the MSSP. Gap: Plant 2 router sessions are invisible (POAM-003).
Corporate Wi-Fi uses certificate-based authentication. Gap: Plant 2 has 2 consumer-grade access points on the plant network installed by maintenance in 2023.
Company phones and tablets are enrolled in mobile device management with encryption and remote wipe before they can reach email or the ERP.
POL-05 limits use of personal devices and external systems for company data. Gap: OEM laptops still connect directly to Plant 2 HMIs during service visits.
Only Marketing publishes to the website and customer download portal; FCI and drawings are never posted publicly. Contract and portal postings are reviewed before release.
Awareness and training requirements are set in POL-05 and the training calendar, approved 2026-09-15.

Office staff complete annual awareness training (96% in 2026) and quarterly phishing simulations (June 2026 click rate 6.9%). Gap: production workers receive orientation-level content only, and field technicians receive no training on utility access rules (POAM-013).
Insider threat indicators are covered in manager training. Gap: not yet covered for production supervisors.
Role-based training exists for administrators and the security team. Gap: plant controls staff, test engineers, and the product software team have no role-based security training (POAM-013).
Logging requirements are in POL-03 and the draft logging and monitoring standard STD-02 (due 2027-01-31).

Identity, cloud control plane, ERP audit, firewall, VPN, EDR, and Plant 1 OT sensor events are logged and sent to the SIEM. Gap: the MES at both plants, the historians, Plant 2 OT, and the integration platform's message logs are not collected (POAM-007).
evidence: SIEM source list; P07 AU-2 test

implementation_statement: Collected records include time, source, user, event type, and outcome; the SIEM normalizes fields.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The MSSP reviews and correlates collected events 24x7; the Security Manager reviews the monthly report and ERP super-user activity. Gap: no review of MES or OT events; the monthly ERP review was skipped in May 2026 (POAM-007).
evidence: MSSP monthly reports; ERP review sign-offs

implementation_statement: Review, analysis, and reporting are integrated in the SIEM with automated correlation rules.
IT systems synchronize to the corporate time source. Gap: Plant 2 OT devices and the Plant 2 MES drift up to 4 minutes, which weakens investigation timelines.
Cloud and SIEM logs are written to a locked log archive in the shared services account; only 2 security staff can change retention.
SIEM keeps 1 year searchable; the log archive keeps 3 years; ERP audit tables keep 7 years for export records.
Audit generation is enabled on all cloud services, the identity provider, the ERP, and firewalls. Gap: not enabled on the Plant 2 MES database (POAM-007).
The co-sourced internal audit firm assesses controls annually; the 2026 assessment covered 33 controls (P07).

Information exchanges with the EDI provider, bank, and ERP vendor are covered by contracts. Gap: internal exchanges between the EPSP and plant systems, the PLM vault, and the Plant 2 MES are not documented, and the Plant 2 domain trust has no written terms (POAM-001).
The POA&M (P07) tracks every weakness with an owner and dates and is reviewed monthly by the COO and quarterly by the audit committee.
The COO accepted continued operation of the EPSP with conditions on 2026-09-15 (section 4.2).
Continuous monitoring covers cloud posture, vulnerability scans, MSSP monitoring, and monthly metrics to the COO. Gap: OT and MES metrics are not yet included.
Internal connections between the MES and plant zones at Plant 1 are documented in the OT DMZ design. Gap: Plant 2 internal connections are undocumented.
Configuration management is covered by POL-01 and POL-04; the configuration standard STD-01 is in draft (due 2027-03-31).
Cloud workloads are built from hardened images with organization guardrails; Plant 1 OT DMZ components have documented baselines. Gap: no baselines for the Plant 2 MES, kiosks, or HMIs (POAM-010).
evidence: Image pipeline; guardrail list; Plant 1 baseline document

implementation_statement: ERP and integration changes go through the change advisory board with test evidence. Gap: MES recipe-reference and interface changes at Plant 2 are made without tickets; 4 of 15 sampled MES changes had no record (POAM-010).
Security impact is considered for ERP changes at the change advisory board. Gap: not for plant-side changes.
Production changes to cloud workloads require pipeline deployment by authorized engineers. Gap: Plant 2 MES administrators make direct production changes.
Benchmark-based settings are enforced on cloud virtual machines and Windows endpoints; drift reports run monthly. Gap: Plant 2 kiosks and the MES server are unhardened.

Unneeded services are disabled on cloud workloads and Plant 1 OT DMZ servers; USB storage is blocked on office endpoints and Plant 1 HMIs. Gap: Plant 2 kiosks and HMIs allow USB storage and run remote desktop services (POAM-010).
evidence: GPO and endpoint policy; P07 CM-7 test

implementation_statement: IT assets are inventoried in the configuration management database; Plant 1 OT assets are inventoried by the passive OT sensor. Gap: the Plant 2 OT inventory is about 50% complete, and unsupported systems are not flagged (POAM-008).
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-032, G-033)

implementation_statement: The inventory updates automatically for IT endpoints and cloud resources. Gap: Plant 2 changes are not captured.
Software licenses are tracked for ERP, CAD, and MES products.
Users cannot install software on office endpoints; requests go through the service desk.
Contingency planning is required by POL-03 and the contingency and recovery standard STD-07 (due 2026-12-31).

An IT disaster recovery plan (2024) covers the ERP and integration platform. Gaps: it does not cover the MES, the Plant 2 server room, OT dependencies, or the BIA recovery order from P05, and it names people who have left (POAM-005).
evidence: DR plan 2024; P05 BIA; P07 CP-2 test
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-052, G-099)

implementation_statement: Planned: contingency role training for IT, plant, and Digital Services staff after STD-07 is issued (2027-02).
A file-level ERP restore was tested in 2025. Gap: no full ERP or landing zone recovery test, no MES restore test, and no OT restore test at either plant (POAM-005, POAM-006).
evidence: Restore test record 2025-04; P07 CP-4 test
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-064, G-050)

implementation_statement: Backups are stored in the backup account in a second region with separate administrator credentials.
The ERP can be rebuilt in the second region from infrastructure templates. Gap: never exercised; the MES has no alternate processing capability.
SD-WAN uses two carriers at HQ and Plant 1 and cellular failover at Plant 2.

ERP database: 7-day point-in-time recovery plus daily copies to the backup account (35-day write-once retention). Plant 1 MES and controller programs: nightly backups in the OT DMZ with weekly offline copies. Gap: the Plant 2 MES backs up to a local disk only, and Plant 2 controller programs are copied by hand (POAM-006).
evidence: Backup job reports; retention lock settings; P07 CP-9 test

implementation_statement: Backup jobs are checked daily for completion. Gap: integrity is not verified by restore, except the 2025 file-level test.
Recovery procedures exist for the ERP and integration platform. Gap: no reconstitution procedure for the MES or for a full landing zone rebuild; recovery times are unproven (POAM-005).
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-100, G-103)

implementation_statement: Identification and authentication rules are in POL-02, approved 2026-09-15.

All office users have unique identities in the identity provider. MES users authenticate with badge and PIN. Gaps: Plant 2 MES supervisor override accounts and HMI operator logins are shared (POAM-004).

MFA with FIDO2 security keys protects the 18 cloud, identity, and domain administrators; other privileged accounts use push MFA with number matching. Gap: MES administrator and OT engineering workstation accounts have no MFA (POAM-016).
evidence: Conditional access policy; P07 IA-2(1) test

implementation_statement: All office users authenticate with MFA (push with number matching) for email, ERP, VPN, and cloud consoles.
The identity provider uses replay-resistant protocols for all network sign-ins.
Office endpoints authenticate to the network with device certificates. Gap: Plant 2 has no device authentication on the plant network.
Identifiers are unique and never reused for office users. Gap: Plant 2 MES badge numbers are reused after terminations.

Passwords follow the authenticator standard (14 characters, banned list); service account secrets for cloud workloads are vaulted. Gaps: shared HMI and supervisor passwords have not changed since 2024 at Plant 2; the Plant 2 MES service account password dates from 2019 (POAM-002, POAM-004).
evidence: Authenticator standard; vault inventory; P07 IA-5 test

implementation_statement: Non-organizational users (ERP vendor support, auditors) get named guest identities in the identity provider with MFA and expiry.

The security team and MSSP are trained. Gap: plant managers, controls staff, and the crisis management team have had no incident training (POAM-011).
An IT ransomware tabletop was held in 2025. Gap: no OT or crisis management exercise; next exercises are scheduled 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-19 (POAM-011).

The MSSP triages alerts 24x7 and isolates endpoints; the Security Manager runs incidents under the IT plan. Gap: no OT playbook, no manual production procedures at Plant 2, and no evidence preservation procedure for OT (POAM-011).
evidence: Incident log; P07 IR-4 sample of 10 incidents
regulatory_driver: None binding; CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-086, G-097)

implementation_statement: Incidents are tracked in the service management tool with a security category; 41 incidents were logged in the 12 months to 2026-06-30.

POL-03 requires reporting to the Security Manager and sets external notices through the notification matrix (P08). Gap: the 24- and 48-hour utility incident notices and the 1-business-day access notice have no tested procedure; 2 access notices were late in 2026 (POAM-018).
evidence: POL-03; obligations register; P07 IR-6 interviews
regulatory_driver: Utility addendum sec. 1 (CIP-013-2 R1.2.1 flow-down; P03 G-127); CSF 2.0 benchmark (P03 G-095)

Electronic visitor records at HQ and Plant 1. Gap: paper log at Plant 2.
Standby generators and UPS cover both server rooms, the Plant 1 OT DMZ cabinet, and test system controls; tested monthly.
